newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe attacks "rigid sanctions" after EMU.
newsitem.headline: Juppe attacks "rigid sanctions" after EMU.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, in an apparent attack on Germany's proposal for a budget stability pact, said European monetary union must not be run according to numerical norms, accompanied by rigid sanctions.

"We will not submit either to numerical norms accompanied by rigid and automatic sanctions, nor to the central bank, whose independence we must respect in that it aims to guarantee price stability but which cannot be a substitute for political power," Juppe said.

Talks on a stability pact to go into effect after the launch of a single European currency have run into trouble over German demands that countries face automatic fines if their deficits exceed three percent of gross domestic product, the maximum stipulated in the Maastricht treaty on European union.
Germany wants a numerical definition of when and how such sanctions would be imposed and what temporary circumstances would allow an exemption to the sanctions.
Other countries favour letting finance ministers decide whether a country's economic situation could exempt it from the sanctions.
